synopsis: 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4), together with 1926.602(a)(9)(ii), is in force for US construction [f2762]. Chapter 3 and the glossary agree that an obstructed rear view requires a reverse alarm or an observer, with the alarm audible above surrounding noise [f2763, f2764, f15505]. Chapter 3 additionally reports that interpretations allow camera and radar alternatives [f2763]. These rules prescribe neither a numeric range nor automatic braking, so they do not themselves supply those acceptance criteria for a collision-mitigation system [f2765].

relations.note: Both require a reverse alarm or observer when rear visibility is obstructed.
Glossary places the audibility requirement within the obstructed-view alarm-or-observer rule.
Specifies that the required reverse alarm must exceed surrounding noise.
Clarifies that the alarm-or-observer requirement specifies neither numeric range nor automatic braking.
